decisions_requested.decision: Head 07: dflash262k fails only the TTFT gate, and only in relative terms — +38.54% relative is +16.9 ms absolute (43.7 -> 60.6 ms), the draft's extra prefill pass, against +23.6% sustained decode with byte-identical output. Rule whether the TTFT gate should be absolute-bounded (e.g. <=100 ms) for short prompts. If re-scoped, dflash262k passes every gate materially, which per your stop rule is the evidence threshold for asking Curtis to reopen the 1M memory budget (2.44 GiB shortfall).

Head 07: 5b is now QUALIFIED OPT-IN per your V11 mapping. Two qualified opt-in profiles (longprefix, potentially dflash262k) plus canonical now exist; if both are retained, profile-selection routing (who chooses per-job) needs an owner and a mechanism — flagging for the next ruling, not proposing scope.

risks: The dflash TTFT measurement is short-prompt only (43-token qualify prompt); TTFT at long prompt lengths was not measured in this bounded goal and the draft prefill cost scales with input length.
5b QUALIFIED OPT-IN and dflash262k are separate profiles measured separately; combining them (dflash + prefix caching) is unmeasured and out of scope.
